title: Sensitive GPS data collection
description: Live GPS coordinates are highly sensitive personal data that may be collected without strict necessity for the stated functionality.

title: Excessive frequency of GPS transmission
description: Regular interval GPS transmissions may be more frequent than functionally needed for the stated purpose.

title: Fine-grained location data disclosure
description: Live GPS coordinates provide fine-grained location granularity that may exceed functional requirements.

title: Revealing location attributes
description: GPS coordinates are revealing attributes that can be used to identify and track the data subject's movements.

title: Individual distinguishability through GPS
description: Live GPS coordinates can make the data subject distinguishable from others, reducing anonymity.

title: Linking through quasi-identifier GPS data
description: GPS coordinates combined with other data (time, device ID) can serve as quasi-identifiers to link to specific individuals.

title: Profiling through movement patterns
description: GPS data can be analyzed to profile individual movement patterns and habits.

title: Unawareness of GPS tracking
description: Children may not be aware that their live GPS coordinates are being continuously transmitted and processed.

title: Lack of control over data collection
description: Data subjects may lack control over how, when, and for how long their GPS data is collected and processed.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (live GPS coordinates) is processed than is actually needed for the stated functionality.

title: Insufficient data subject controls
description: Support for data subject rights regarding GPS data collection and processing may be lacking.

title: Location data used for user linking
description: Location pings from mobile app backend can be used to link user identity across sessions or devices, enabling tracking of individual movement patterns.

title: Location data combined with other data for identification
description: Location data combined with other user data (device ID, time, etc.) can serve as quasi-identifiers to identify individuals.

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The mobile app backend processes and forwards location data that can identify or be used to identify users.

title: Location data as unique identifier
description: Location pings can serve as unique references to identify users, especially when combined with device identifiers.

title: Sensitive location data disclosed unnecessarily
description: Location data is a sensitive personal data type that should only be collected and processed when strictly required for geofencing functionality.

title: Excessive volume of location data processed
description: All location pings may be forwarded to geofencing engine even when not all are needed for zone entry/exit detection.

title: Location data propagated to external service
description: Location data is propagated from mobile app backend to geofencing engine service where it may be accessible beyond functional requirements.

title: Users unaware of location processing
description: Users may not be aware that their location pings are being forwarded to the geofencing engine for processing.

title: Lack of user control over location processing
description: Users may not have control to customize or opt-out of location data being forwarded to geofencing engine.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Location data may be more processed than actually needed for the geofencing functionality of zone entry/exit detection.

title: Location data accessible to multiple parties
description: Geofencing engine may have access to location data from multiple users, potentially exceeding functional requirements.

title: Sensitive location data collected
description: Zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) contain sensitive location information that may be more sensitive than functionally required for basic geofencing functionality.

title: Excessive volume of location data
description: Zone definitions may include more location data than functionally needed for the geofencing alert engine to operate.

title: Unnecessary data treatment
description: Zone definitions may be further analyzed or enriched beyond what is necessary for the basic geofencing functionality.

title: Data shared with predetermined parties
description: Zone definitions may be made accessible to more parties than functionally necessary for the geofencing system.

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The system requests and processes identified location data (home, school, friend's house) which may contain personally identifiable information.

title: Revealing attributes in zone data
description: Zone definitions contain revealing attributes that support identification of data subjects (e.g., home location reveals residence, school reveals education status).

title: Quasi-identifier combining for linking
description: Zone definitions combined with other data (e.g., timestamps, user actions) can serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to specific individuals.

title: Profiling an individual through location patterns
description: Zone data can be analyzed for patterns to link data to that individual, revealing daily routines and habits.

title: Unawareness of processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their zone definitions are being processed and used for geofencing functionality.

title: Lack of control over data processing
description: Users may lack control to set preferences or consent in how their zone definitions are processed.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (zone definitions) is processed than is actually needed for the geofencing functionality.

title: Child identifier in location notification
description: The geofencing engine may include the child's unique identifier in the arrival/departure notification sent to the parent, which could be used to identify the specific child being tracked.
assumptions: The notification includes child identification information

title: Data disclosed to more parties than necessary
description: The notification may be accessible to more parties than functionally necessary for the geofencing alert functionality, potentially exposing child location data to unintended recipients.
assumptions: The notification could be forwarded or accessible by additional parties beyond the parent

title: Child unawareness of location tracking
description: The child may not be aware that their location is being tracked and that arrival/departure notifications are being sent to the parent, which could impact informed consent.
assumptions: The child is not explicitly informed about the tracking and notification process

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The notification may include more personal data than is actually needed for the geofencing alert functionality, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: The notification includes child identification and location data beyond what is strictly required for alerting

title: Location data detected through communications
description: The arrival/departure notification communication itself could be used to detect the child's presence in or absence from the defined zone, potentially revealing location patterns.
assumptions: The notification is transmitted and could be intercepted or observed

title: Location data used as identifier for child
description: Child's location data is processed and shared, which can serve as a unique reference to identify the child's identity and movements.
assumptions: Location data is collected and transmitted to the mobile app backend.

title: Location as revealing attribute
description: Location data is a revealing attribute that can be used to identify the child's whereabouts and potentially infer other personal information.
assumptions: Location data is transmitted to the mobile app backend.

title: Data disclosed to more parties than functionally needed
description: Child's location data is shared with secondary guardians (grandparent, relative) who may not be functionally necessary for the core purpose of the system.
assumptions: The system allows sharing with any secondary guardian without strict functional necessity.

title: Child unaware of location sharing
description: The child data subject may not be aware that their location is being collected and shared with secondary guardians.
assumptions: The child does not have visibility into who has access to their location data.

title: Child lacks control over data sharing preferences
description: The child does not have control to set preferences or consent on how their location data is processed and shared with third parties.
assumptions: The child is not involved in the consent or preference setting process for location sharing.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Location data may be more personal data than is actually needed for the functional purpose of sharing with a secondary guardian.
assumptions: The system collects and processes location data beyond what is strictly required for the intended function.

title: Location data can be linked through quasi-identifier
description: Location data combined with other data (time, device ID, etc.) can serve as a quasi-identifier to link the child's movements to their identity.
assumptions: Location data is combined with other identifying information in the system.

title: Revealing attributes in live location data
description: Live location data contains revealing attributes that can support the identification of the child data subject, as location data can be used to identify individuals.
assumptions: Assumes the live location data is not anonymized or aggregated before sharing.

title: Excessive exposure to secondary guardian
description: Personal data (live location) is made accessible to a secondary guardian party that may not be functionally necessary for the core functionality of the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Assumes the secondary guardian access is not strictly required for the primary functionality of the app.

title: Sensitive data type disclosure
description: Live location data is a highly sensitive personal data type that should only be collected and processed when strictly required for the system's functional goals.
assumptions: Assumes live location is not strictly required for the app's core functionality.

title: Fine-grained location data disclosure
description: Live location data is disclosed at a fine-grained level of granularity (real-time or frequent updates) that may be more detailed than functionally needed.
assumptions: Assumes the granularity of location data sharing exceeds what is functionally required.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data (live location) is processed and shared than is actually needed for the functional goals of the mobile app backend system.
assumptions: Assumes the data minimization principle should be applied to this data flow.

title: Unawareness of data disclosure
description: The child data subject may not be aware that their live location is being shared with a secondary guardian, which impacts their understanding of data processing.
assumptions: Assumes the child may not have explicit knowledge of this data sharing.

title: Data shared with predetermined advertising partner
description: Personal data is made accessible to a predetermined set of parties (advertising/analytics partner) that is known up front and static. While this is a known party, the sharing of aggregated analytics to third-party advertising partners may exceed functional necessity for the app's core functionality.
assumptions: The advertising partner is a predetermined, static set of parties

title: Users unaware of data sharing with advertising partners
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their usage and engagement analytics are being shared with external advertising/analytics partners to fund the free tier of the application.
assumptions: Users may not have explicit knowledge of this data sharing practice

title: Potentially sensitive data types disclosed
description: Usage and engagement analytics may include data types that are perceived as sensitive (e.g., usage patterns, engagement metrics) and should only be collected when strictly required for the app's functionality.
assumptions: Some usage/engagement data may be more sensitive than functionally required
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if aggregated data contains sensitive information

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data may be processed than is actually needed for the functional goal of funding the free tier through advertising partnerships.
assumptions: The data collected may exceed what is strictly necessary for the advertising funding purpose

title: Location data contains unique identifier
description: The child's current location data may contain unique identifiers (e.g., GPS coordinates, device ID) that can be used to identify the child uniquely.
assumptions: Assumes location data includes precise GPS coordinates or device identifiers

title: Excessive location data granularity
description: The location data sent may be more granular than functionally required for a check-in/SOS message, potentially including precise coordinates beyond what is needed.
assumptions: Assumes the system collects precise location data rather than approximate location

title: Child unaware of location data processing
description: The child may not be fully aware that their location data is being collected, processed, and potentially stored beyond the immediate SOS/check-in purpose.
assumptions: Assumes the child may not understand the full implications of sharing location data

title: Location data accessible to more parties than necessary
description: The location data may be accessible to more parties than functionally required for the check-in/SOS purpose, potentially including third-party services or analytics.
assumptions: Assumes the mobile app backend may share or expose location data to additional services

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more location data than is actually needed for the functional purpose of a check-in/SOS message, violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: Assumes the system collects and processes more location data than strictly necessary

title: Location data can be detected by third parties
description: The location data transmitted in the SOS/check-in message may be detectable by third parties who intercept or monitor the communication.
assumptions: Assumes the communication channel may not be fully encrypted or monitored by third parties
